meaning: A network that predicts the next state of the scene from the current state and an action.
The model's description of the whole scene at one instant, as opposed to observation.state, the six measured joint angles.
A chain of predictions made by feeding a world model its own output together with the next action.
One action sequence being tried inside a world model during planning.
How many actions ahead each candidate looks during planning.
A network that turns a frame or clip into a smaller set of numbers.
A network that redraws pixels from an encoder's output.
An encoder and decoder trained together so the decoder can rebuild the pixels from the encoder's much smaller grid of numbers.
One vector a transformer processes; here, one position in the compressed grid.
Said of a network whose weights are not updated while the rest of the model trains.
Generating one token at a time, each conditioned on the ones before.
A policy that maps camera images and an instruction to actions; section 5 covers it.
The next several actions returned in one answer; defined in section 3.
A network that works out which actions would produce a given piece of video.
The packaged container NVIDIA ships for serving a model; its support matrix prints minimum GPU memory per device.
A 16-bit number format that takes 2 bytes per weight.
An 8-bit number format that takes 1 byte per weight.
The binary gigabyte, slightly larger than a GB.
NVIDIA's current video-generating world model family (Super, Nano, Edge), released at the end of May 2026.
NVIDIA's world-action model described in a November 2026 whitepaper; code announced for December 2026, not yet downloadable.
NVIDIA's February 2026 world-action model, the paper that coined the term.
Meta's latent world model that takes actions: a frozen video encoder plus a trained predictor, used for planning.
A small latent world model of about 15M parameters that keeps one vector per frame.
The internal code an encoder makes of a frame or clip: a grid or vector of numbers. Both families have one; the pixel family's is built to be decoded back into pixels.
World models that predict the next camera frames, through a reconstruction code that a decoder turns back into pixels.
World models that predict the encoder's summary of the next frames and never draw a picture.
A latent that must keep enough to rebuild every pixel, which is what a video generator predicts.
In a latent world model, the network that takes the current latent and an action and outputs the next latent in one pass.
A design that predicts the encoder's summary of the future and never the picture; section 7 covers it.
Choosing an action by imagining many candidates in a world model, scoring each against a goal and running the best.
One run of a generator's transformer over all its tokens, cleaning them a little; a video generator makes tens of them per clip. Section 4 builds diffusion and flow matching.
Training a predictor so that every guess starts from the true history and never from its own earlier guesses.
The failure in which an encoder scored against encodings gives every input the same vector; section 7 covers what prevents it.
Running a policy so that each action changes what the policy sees next.
One model that outputs future video and the robot's actions together, so the world model is the policy and nothing is searched.
A small block of neighbouring grid positions that becomes one token.
Computing through the predictor which way to change the candidate actions, where a search only samples them.
Meta's latent world model for robot arms: predictors of 22M to 8B parameters on a frozen 2B encoder.
Learning by trial and error from a score; section 8 covers it.
